title: Object equality
summary: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object.
introduction: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("returns a point", () => { const point = { x: 2, y: 4 }; expect(point).toEqual({ x: 2, y: 4 }); });
blocks.title: Object equality

blocks.text: The test passes because both coordinates match.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change y in the expected object.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not confuse equal fields with the same object identity.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
